newsitem.title: USA: Canada ready to assist in Peru, Axworthy says.
newsitem.headline: Canada ready to assist in Peru, Axworthy says.

text.p: Canadian foreign affairs minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Friday Canada would agree to help resolve the hostage situation in Peru if asked, but no specific plans had been made.
"We're prepared to help in any way," Axworthy told reporters after speaking to a class at the John F. Kennedy School of Government at Harvard University.
But he said Canada had no specific plans for helping to bring an end to the 52-day standoff, aside from the continued mediation by Canada's ambassador to Peru, Anthony Vincent.

Vincent told reporters earlier this week in Toronto that Peru is searching for an asylum destination for the Tupac Amaru rebels, who are holding 72 captives in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
One possible destination was Cuba, Vincent said.

Axworthy said the Peruvian guerrillas were raised in his discussions with Cuban President Fidel Castro during his brief trip to Cuba about two weeks ago, but only in broad discussions on how to fight terrorism.
"Within that discussion we talked about what had happened in Peru and the fact that it is another example of how everybody is vulnerable, or virtually everybody is, to these actions," he said.
He also said there were no current plans for Canada to take a broader role in Peru by sending Canadian troops to provide passage for the rebels to another country.
"We have no plans or specific initiatives," he said.

Axworthy, criticised by some U.S. officials for his trip to Cuba, was the highest ranking Canadian to visit the country in two decades. He said his visit has helped open dialogue between Canada and Cuba.

Canadian officials will meet with their Cuban counterparts in Havana in mid-March to discuss how Cuba could embrace specific measures to fight terrorism agreed to by Group of Seven nations at a Paris meeting last summer.
"It's one of the things that I think, as I said to some of the American counterparts, is a plus coming out of the meetings," he said. "We are now engaging the Cubans on these discussions."
